column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls him weary and weak of hands; BSB reverses the description and leaves the hands implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the awaited words as what is “in his mouth”; BSB has what he “has to say”.
The Hebrew repeats Absalom as the speaker; BSB uses “who”.
The Hebrew explicitly says Hushai spoke to Absalom; BSB leaves the addressee implicit.
The Hebrew names Hushai again and describes the men as bitter of soul; BSB uses “He” and “fierce”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the valiant men “sons of valor”; BSB has a soldier and valiant men.
The Hebrew describes his personal participation as his “face” going into battle; BSB says he himself should lead them.
The Hebrew includes David himself with his men in the statement that none will remain; BSB explicitly names only the men.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the LORD commanded the frustration and repeats the LORD as the one bringing disaster; BSB says “purposed” and leaves the second subject implicit.
The Hebrew repeats “thus and thus” for both sets of advice; BSB has “This is what”.

The Hebrew calls her “the woman”; BSB specifies “the man’s wife”.
The Hebrew leaves the searchers unnamed; BSB supplies “The men”.
The Hebrew leaves the departing and ascending groups unnamed; BSB supplies “the men” and “Ahimaaz and Jonathan”. It names David again and says “the water”, where BSB has “the river”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he gave instructions to his house; BSB has “put his affairs in order”.
